data.gender_notes: Manas is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manas is a Sanskrit and Hindi name for mind or intellect. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'manas' which means 'mind'. This name is often used to describe someone who is intelligent, wise, and thoughtful. The name Manas carries the meaning “Mind, Intellect” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Manas usually hope their child will grow to embody mind, intellect and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Manas is a spiritual name in Hinduism that represents the human mind and intellect. It is believed that the mind is the seat of consciousness and the source of all thoughts and emotions. By using this name, one can connect with the divine energy of the mind and cultivate wisdom and knowledge.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Manas' has profound cultural significance in Hinduism and Sanskrit literature. In Hindu mythology, Manas is also the name of the god of memory and intelligence. In various scriptures, Manas is described as a manifestation of the goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and arts. The name Manas is also associated with the concept of 'manvantaras', which is the period between one cosmic creation and the next. The term 'manav' means 'man' and 'antara' means 'interval', suggesting that Manas is the embodiment of consciousness that spans through the different manvantaras.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Manas signifies the higher consciousness or the intellect that plays a crucial role in the spiritual journey of an individual. The Hindu philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga emphasize the importance of developing the intellect through self-study, introspection, and meditation. The name Manas, thus, encourages one to tap into their inner wisdom and seek knowledge and understanding of the ultimate truth of existence. It is a reminder that one must use their mind and intellect wisely to attain spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manas in Sanskrit means 'mind'. It is the seat of consciousness, thought, intellect, and emotions. It is the tool through which we perceive the world and experience reality. In Hindu philosophy, controlling the mind is essential for achieving inner peace and self-realization.
